description: Real-image validation corpus for background removal quality assessment. Masks are classified into four tiers: ground-truth (independently annotated), human-reviewed (manually corrected), reference-model (generated by a model, not ground truth), and synthetic (programmatic fixtures).
license: Pexels License (free for personal and commercial use)

maskClassification.groundTruth: Independently annotated or sourced from a dataset with valid redistribution rights. These are the authoritative quality targets.
maskClassification.humanReviewed: Manually created or corrected and approved for regression use. Higher quality than model-generated but not independently annotated.
maskClassification.referenceModel: Generated by u2netp, IS-Net, BiRefNet, or another model. Use ONLY for drift detection and relative comparison — never claim as absolute quality evidence.
maskClassification.synthetic: Programmatic fixtures for narrow edge-case tests (e.g., solid-color shapes, gradient boundaries). Not representative of real-world segmentation.

metrics.note: Never aggregate all fixtures into one score that hides regressions in hair, fur, or transparency.

corpusGuidelines.groundTruthMaskCreation: Use legally redistributable public datasets, manually annotated fixtures, or model-assisted masks followed by human correction. Distinguish binary segmentation masks from alpha mattes for hair/fur/glass/transparency.
corpusGuidelines.referenceModelUsage: Use ONLY for: detecting implementation drift, comparing preprocessing/postprocessing changes, verifying deterministic behavior, measuring relative model differences. NEVER use to claim absolute segmentation accuracy.
forbiddenClaims: Labeling u2netp outputs as ground truth
Aggregating all fixtures into one score that hides category-specific regressions
Claiming reference-model masks prove absolute segmentation quality
